# RMD Remediation Program — Final Report

**Status:** CLOSED · **Date:** 2026-07-18 · **Result:** 70/80 passed, 10 descoped · **Main HEAD:** `cf639da`

The RMD (Remediation) program was an autonomous DAG pipeline built to fix Zuri's
security-audit findings, run by a tiered agent fleet with a frontier gate, and driven
to completion as a hybrid of pipeline automation + architect-tier (frontier main-loop)
work.

---

## TL;DR (ภาษาไทย) — RWANG pipeline คุ้มไหม?

**1. ประหยัดกว่าไหม?** — *แล้วแต่งาน.* งาน mechanical (sweep / migration / rename /
ใส่ pattern ซ้ำๆ) → **คุ้มชัดเจน**. งาน judgment-heavy (ออกแบบ, แก้ทั้ง codebase, ตัดสินใจ
กำกวม) → **เสมอตัวถึงแพงกว่า** frontier เพราะวน worker→review→rework เฉลี่ย 5.3 รอบ/task
แล้วสุดท้ายหลายตัวก็ต้องให้ frontier ทำเองอยู่ดี. โปรแกรมนี้งาน judgment เยอะ → **~เสมอตัว**.

**2. ประหยัดกว่าเท่าไร?** — pipeline วัดได้ **$111.57** (sonnet review กิน 53%). เฉพาะ task
ที่ผ่านรอบเดียว ≈ **$0.60/task** เทียบกับ frontier ≈ $2–5 → **ถูกกว่า ~3–8 เท่า** เฉพาะงานนั้น.
**local LLM = ฟรี ($0 API** — จ่ายแค่ค่าไฟ GPU). *แต่* ตัวเลขนี้ **ไม่รวม** งาน architect ใน
main-loop (งานยาก ~30 ตัว + orchestration/merge ทั้งหมด — แยกต่างหาก ไม่ได้ log) → ต้นทุนจริง
เป็น **hybrid ไม่ใช่การแทนที่**.

**3. ยุ่งยากในการ setting ไหม?** — *ปานกลาง–ค่อนข้างยุ่ง.* ต้องมี orchestrator (DAG,
`run-dag.mjs`) + backlog YAML + deterministic gates + Ollama/GPU (สำหรับ local) + API
(sonnet/opus) และตอนรันจริง**เจอ bug ใน harness หลายจุด** (auto-commit หล่นงาน, WSL แปลง
path พัง, JSON verdict parse เพี้ยน, worker-commit race). **รอบแรกแพงกว่าเพราะ debug churn;
รอบหลังถูกลงเมื่อ harness นิ่งแล้ว**.

> **สรุปสั้น:** ให้ bot ทำงานซ้ำๆ (mechanical) — คุ้มและ local ฟรี; งานที่ต้องใช้วิจารณญาณ
> เก็บไว้ทำใน frontier main-loop. ตั้งค่าไม่ trivial แต่จ่ายครั้งเดียว.

## 1. Outcome by wave

| Wave | Theme | Passed | Descoped |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Security Hotfix | **32 / 32** | — |
| 2 | Data Integrity | **19 / 21** | B14, B15 |
| 3 | Quality Hardening | **11 / 15** | C13, C14, C15, D05 |
| 4 | Feature Completion | **8 / 12** | E07, E08, E09, E11 |
| — | **Total** | **70 / 80** | **10** |

All work is merged to `main` and CI-verified (Unit Tests · Prisma Schema Validation ·
Edge Bundle Safety · Vercel). No `rmd/*` branches remain.

## 2. What was delivered

- **Security (Wave 1):** session/tenant scoping across all API routes via `withAuth`,
  middleware consolidation, RBAC domain fixes, login rate-limiting (+ cf-connecting-ip),
  and central prefix-based **plan gating** (`FREE<STARTER<PRO<ENTERPRISE`).
- **Data integrity (Wave 2):** `Float→Decimal(12,2)` money, migration baseline, tenant
  FKs, per-tenant customer uniques, and **atomic stock deduction** with transactional
  rollback + an idempotency guard (`Order.stockDeductedAt`) that fixed a real
  double-deduction. Fixed several cross-tenant leaks.
- **Quality (Wave 3):** zod input validation across order/procurement/enrollment/CRM
  routes, an error-leak sweep (no more `err.message` to clients), and a **redis
  version-counter** rewrite that eliminated every `redis.keys()` keyspace scan
  (+ a per-tenant index set that also removed a cross-tenant scan).
- **Features (Wave 4):** Customer-360 LTV/segment service, change-password (API + UI),
  plan-gate application executed on **local LLM**.

## 3. The 10 descoped tasks (rationale, not effort)

Each is recorded in `state.json` with a `skipReason`. They were descoped because they
conflicted with the stack, lacked a data model, or needed live infrastructure — forcing
them would have shipped misleading or unverifiable code.

| Task | Reason |
|---|---|
| B14 / B15 | Hard Prisma enums conflict with tenant-configurable statuses (`systemConfig`) |
| C13–C15 | Repo-pattern hygiene across ~50 routes — **non-security** (the `db.ts` extension already auto-scopes `tenantId`) |
| D05 | A `tsconfig.json` flips Next into TypeScript mode and breaks the Vercel build on a JS codebase |
| E07 | No tenant-subscription-billing data model exists (`Invoice`/`Transaction` are customer-order data) |
| E08 | Multi-part QStash/xlsx/email export — a focused feature initiative, not remediation |
| E09 | E2E (`playwright test`) needs a live app + browser + seeded DB — unverifiable in CI |
| E11 | Live FB/LINE Graph API backfill — production-safety unverifiable without real API |

The mobile app (**E12**) decision: **GO / invest** — greenlit as a separate feature
initiative (see `MOBILE-DECISION.md`).

## 4. Cost & token economics (pipeline)

Source: `docs/remediation/model_stats.jsonl` — 357 `claude -p` subprocess calls across
all runs (including rework/debug churn).

**Total pipeline cost: $111.57** · 553.6k tokens in · 2.30M out · ~$1.59 / passed task

| Tier | Calls | Cost | Share |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sonnet review | 138 | **$59.47** | **53%** |
| Haiku workers | 170 | $32.92 | 30% |
| Opus decision | 31 | $10.51 | 9% |
| Opus final-gate | 8 | $8.67 | 8% |
| Local (Ollama) | 10 | **$0.00** | 0% |

**Rework churn:** 5.3 worker+review calls per passed task; 31 of 70 tasks needed 2–7
attempts, 39 passed first-try.

### Pipeline vs. frontier Claude Code

| | Pipeline (RWANG) | Frontier main-loop |
|---|---|---|
| Per task | worker → gate → **Sonnet review** → rework ×N → Opus gate | read → write → verify, self-reviews |
| Round-trips | **~5.3 / task** | ~1–2 |
| Cheap tier | haiku / local (pennies, local = $0) | none |
| Hard tasks | often **blocks → handed to frontier** (sunk cost) | done in 1–2 passes |

**Verdict for this program (judgment-heavy mix): ~break-even to slightly worse than
pure frontier.**
- **Pipeline wins** on mechanical bulk (route sweeps, planGate, cache) — 39 first-try
  passes at ~$0.60 each vs ~$2–5 for a frontier. Local LLM = $0 API.
- **Pipeline loses** on judgment-heavy work — the worker→review→rework ladder is
  overhead; ~30 tasks reworked/blocked then finished in the main loop anyway.

> **Caveat:** the $111.57 is the *pipeline only*. Architect-tier work (the hard ~30
> tasks + all orchestration, merging, and conflict resolution) ran in the frontier main
> loop and is **not** in `model_stats.jsonl`. Total program cost ≈ pipeline + a
> comparable/larger main-loop figure. This was a **hybrid**, not a replacement.

## 5. Lessons learned

1. **Triage before dispatch.** Route mechanical/repetitive work to the pipeline
   (maximize local-LLM use = free); keep design/judgment/whole-codebase work in the
   frontier main loop. Don't expect the pipeline to finish ambiguous tasks — budget for
   it to block and hand off.
2. **Sonnet review is the cost driver (53%), not the cheap worker.** The savings lever
   is fewer rework rounds.
3. **The frontier gate earns its keep — as consistency/auditability.** It caught the
   atomicity swallow, migration drift, incomplete plan-gating, and cross-tenant leaks.
   A frontier main loop self-reviews and catches the same classes, but the gate makes it
   systematic and traceable.
4. **Descope honestly.** 10 tasks were better descoped than forced — a documented
   won't-do beats misleading (E07) or unverifiable (E09/E11) code, or a build-breaking
   change (D05).
5. **Harden the harness mid-flight.** A silent auto-commit bug dropped every passed
   task's work (staged-but-uncommitted) until fixed; a staged-index assertion now fails
   loudly instead of passing silently.
6. **Local LLM works end-to-end** once the GPU was repaired — `sushirl`/`ornith` passed
   gate + review, and the review layer correctly caught a local model's hallucinated
   plan names. Local inference = $0 API.
